notable_absence.finding: Step 11 ('(Optional) To add additional regular expressions to the list of exception patterns, repeat the previous steps') describes a repeatable one-to-many sub-list (exception patterns) nested inside a single exception tokenizer, the same cardinality gap already flagged in create-custom-analyzer.json's notable_absence (there for character/token filters against the analyzer). The registry still has no predicate or datatype property for 'zero/one-or-more of X per Y', so this record captures containment via hasInternalComponent-equivalent phrasing in prose only, not as a separate relation.

cross_component_finding: This page is the clearest evidence in the batch that hasInternalComponent composition is RECURSIVE, not just a flat analyzer-to-three-component-types shape: an Exception Tokenizer itself contains another tokenizer ('Tokenizer for Remaining Input') as an internal sub-component, one level deeper than the analyzer-to-tokenizer containment stated on create-custom-analyzer.json. The same promoted predicate models both levels correctly with no strain, which is a positive finding about hasInternalComponent's generality, but it also means a naive query for 'components of a custom analyzer' would need to walk hasInternalComponent transitively to reach the exception tokenizer's wrapped tokenizer - the registry has no transitive/closure annotation on this predicate. Also notable: the page states a closed, numbered enumeration ('2 types of custom tokenizers') exactly the shape isSubtypeOf was minted for in an earlier round (Composite Vector Index / GSI), reused here for regexp and exception tokenizers.
